prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: COc1cc2c(cc1OC)C(=O)C(CC1CCN(Cc3ccccc3)CC1)C2
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL4078

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of electric eel AChE using acetylthiocholine iodide as substrate preincubated for 5 mins followed by substrate addition measured at 1 to 3 mins time interval by Ellman's method
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Electrophorus electricus

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of electric eel AChE using acetylthiocholine iodide as substrate incubated for 15 to 20 mins by Ellman's method
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Electrophorus electricus

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call":"COMMENSURABLE","confidence":0.84,"error_class":"none","reason":"Both assays use the same electric eel AChE source, acetylthiocholine substrate, and Ellman readout, with only modest timing differences unlikely to shift IC50 by more than 0.3 log units."}
